abstract: This study examines the adoption patterns of ChatGPT among workers in occupations exposed to AI technology. The research finds significant demographic disparities in adoption, with younger, male, and higher-achieving workers leading usage rates. The unequal distribution of ChatGPT adoption threatens to exacerbate existing labor market inequalities between demographic groups.
keyFindings: Approximately 50% of workers in occupations exposed to ChatGPT have adopted the technology.
Younger workers show higher adoption rates of ChatGPT compared to older workers.
Male workers are significantly more likely to use ChatGPT for work than female workers, with women 16 percentage points less likely to adopt.
Higher-achieving workers lead in ChatGPT adoption relative to their peers.
qualifiers: Study focuses on workers in exposed occupations; generalizability to non-exposed occupations or different labor markets unclear.
